label: Tomato — Healthy
symptoms: No visible lesions or discoloration.
Leaves are uniformly green with normal venation.
treatment: Maintain consistent watering at the base to keep foliage dry.
Rotate crops yearly and avoid overhead irrigation.
Continue scouting weekly for early signs of disease.

label: Tomato — Early Blight
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on lower leaves.
Yellow halos around lesions, leaves drop prematurely.
Stem lesions may appear near the soil line.
treatment: Remove and destroy affected leaves — do not compost.
Apply a copper-based or chlorothalonil fungicide every 7–10 days.
Mulch around the base to prevent soil splash onto foliage.
Rotate away from tomato/potato/eggplant for at least 2 seasons.

label: Tomato — Late Blight
symptoms: Irregular water-soaked greyish-green lesions on leaves.
White fuzzy mold on leaf undersides in humid conditions.
Rapid collapse of foliage, dark lesions on stems and fruit.
treatment: Remove severely affected plants to halt spread.
Spray a protectant fungicide containing mancozeb or copper preventively.
Avoid overhead watering; improve airflow by staking and pruning.
Harvest healthy fruit promptly during outbreaks.

label: Tomato — Leaf Mold
symptoms: Pale yellow patches on upper leaf surfaces.
Olive-green to grey fuzzy mold on leaf undersides.
Leaves curl and drop in severe cases.
treatment: Lower humidity — improve ventilation in greenhouses.
Remove infected leaves and avoid overhead watering.
Apply copper or chlorothalonil fungicide at first signs.

label: Tomato — Bacterial Spot
symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves with yellow halos.
Spots turn angular and may coalesce, defoliating the plant.
Raised scabby lesions on green fruit.
treatment: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants.
Apply copper-based bactericide preventively; add mancozeb for resistance management.
Avoid working with plants when wet to limit spread.

label: Potato — Healthy
symptoms: Uniform green foliage with no lesions.
Normal tuber development and canopy growth.
treatment: Hill soil around stems to protect developing tubers.
Scout weekly and manage aphids that transmit viruses.
Use certified seed potatoes next season.

label: Potato — Early Blight
symptoms: Bullseye-patterned brown lesions on lower leaves.
Yellowing around spots; older leaves affected first.
Sunken dark spots may appear on tubers.
treatment: Remove infected foliage and destroy crop debris after harvest.
Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb fungicide on a 7–10 day schedule.
Ensure balanced nitrogen — stressed plants are more susceptible.

label: Potato — Late Blight
symptoms: Dark greasy-looking lesions spreading rapidly on leaves and stems.
White mold on the underside of leaves in humid weather.
Reddish-brown firm rot on tubers.
treatment: Destroy infected plants immediately — including tubers.
Apply systemic fungicides (e.g. cymoxanil + mancozeb) preventively.
Plant resistant cultivars and use certified seed.

label: Apple — Scab
symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety lesions on leaves and fruit.
Infected leaves yellow and drop early.
Cracked corky spots on fruit surface.
treatment: Rake and destroy fallen leaves to remove overwintering inoculum.
Apply fungicides (captan or myclobutanil) from green tip through petal fall.
Prune for airflow and plant scab-resistant cultivars.

label: Grape — Black Rot
symptoms: Tan circular lesions on leaves with dark borders.
Black pinhead fruiting bodies within leaf spots.
Fruit shrivels into hard black mummies.
treatment: Remove mummified berries and infected canes during dormancy.
Apply protectant fungicides (mancozeb, myclobutanil) from bud break until veraison.
Improve canopy airflow through summer pruning.

label: Unknown class
symptoms: The system has no detailed notes for this class yet.
treatment: Consult a local agricultural extension officer for a definitive diagnosis.
Isolate the plant to prevent potential spread while investigating.
